column1: # DIEFFENBACHSTRASSE 58a — THE THIRTY-THREE-YEAR GAP IS NOW BRIDGED, AND THE OCR WAS HIDING THE BRIDGE.
# Berliner Adressbuch, ZLB record 34115495. Read 10 October 2026. Work list row 250.
# WHAT THE ROW HAD: PAUL LEIPHOLZ, Schlosser, S 59 Dieffenbachstraße 58, in the 1924 volume. KLARA
# LEIPHOLZ, PUTZMACHERIN, SW 29 Dieffenbachstraße 58, in the 1957 and 1959 post-war Namenteil. Same
# street, same number, THIRTY-THREE YEARS AND A WAR APART, and nothing in between.
# ---------------- WHAT IS NEW: THE YEARS IN BETWEEN ----------------
*** PAUL LEIPHOLZ IS AT DIEFFENBACHSTRASSE 58a IN 1941, 1942 AND 1943 ***
column2: 1941 Namenteil: "— Paul Schlosser SW 29 Dieffenbachstr 58a", READ AT THE IMAGE in Fraktur. 1942 Namenteil: the same line in the same run. 1943 TEIL III, the STREET section: the Dieffenbachstraße page lists house 58a, owner Dr. K. TEMP, Wirtschaftsprüfer of Halensee, manager E. Dahms — and among the tenants, *** "LEIPHOLZ, P., SCHLOSSER". ***

column1: SO THE HOUSEHOLD HOLDS THE HOUSE FROM 1924 TO 1959 AT LEAST
column2: 1924 Paul at 58 · 1941, 1942, 1943 Paul at 58a · 1957 and 1959 Klara at 58. THIRTY-FIVE YEARS ACROSS THE WAR, in a street in Kreuzberg. The row could only say "thirty-three years apart"; the gap is now four sightings narrower and the war years are covered.

column1: and the postal district change is confirmed rather than assumed
column2: the row reasoned that S 59 and SW 29 are the same place under Berlin's renumbering. 1941 and 1942 PRINT SW 29 against the same house, seventeen years after S 59 and sixteen before Klara's SW 29. The reasoning holds and is now witnessed.

column1: # ---------------- *** AND THE FULL-TEXT SEARCH MISSED THE BEST YEAR *** ----------------
A SEARCH FOR LEIPHOLZ + DIEFFENBACH ACROSS THE WHOLE RUN RETURNS 1924, 1928 AND 1942 — AND NOT 1941
column2: 1941 was found only by READING THE LEIPHOLZ RUN AS A RUN, headword to next surname, which is the instrument this archive arrived at in September for exactly this reason. The 1941 OCR renders the street "Diessenbachsir" and the search slides past it.

column1: and the house number was wrong in the text layer for every year
column2: the OCR reads "68a" in 1941 and 1942. THE IMAGE SAYS 58a — a Fraktur 5 read as a 6, the same class of error as the Kreuzberg Fraktur 4 read as a 1 on 8 October. Had the number been taken from the text layer this file would have invented a second house on the same street and lost the continuity it exists to show.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH ----------------
IT DOES NOT MAKE THEM KIN TO ANYONE HERE
column2: Paul and Klara Leipholz are a Kreuzberg household sharing a surname variant with this family. NOTHING JOINS THEM TO JACOB, and this file does not. What it establishes is that they are ONE household and not two coincidences — the same trade-less surname at one address across thirty-five years, with a Schlosser and later a Putzmacherin in it.

column1: and the milliner detail still stands as a reason to look, not a finding
column2: KLARA IS A PUTZMACHERIN — a milliner — and the Leibholz trade in Berlin was hats: Auguste a Modistin, Samuel selling Hüte en gros, Kurt a Hutmacher. A shared rare-ish surname and a shared trade is a reason to keep looking and is not a relationship.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT IS NOW REACHABLE AND WAS NOT ----------------
the 1943 house list for 58a, which came free with the street page
column2: Owner Dr. K. TEMP (Halensee, Halenseestr. 12), manager E. DAHMS. Tenants: Bozan · Casimir · Fettin · Gellert · Groh · Grulke · Heinrich · Kapitke · Koltermann · Konopke · Lehmann · LEIPHOLZ · Matteres · Martin · Mittmann · Neitzel · Neumann · Nickel · Pfeiffer · Reimer · Rosenberg · Rosenheimich · Schlemonat · Schubert · Stein · Stolle · Ulbrich · Ränder. A Berlin house list of 1943 is a document in its own right and is recorded whole.

KLARA has NO wartime entry under Leipholz in any volume 1939-1943 — checked year by year and the answer is zero every time. She appears only after the war. Whether she was in the flat and simply not the householder, or arrived later, is not established.
